This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held. Persistent vulnerabilities in the U.S.
air system are laid bare after yesterday's nationwide ground stop. Thousands of flights
remain cancelled and delayed today. Federal officials say a contractor made an error while
upgrading an old telecommunication line. In a statement, L3Harris says it's been modernizing
infrastructure in coordination with the FAA and it supports an investigation into what went wrong.
Mary Schiavo, a former inspector general at the Transportation Department, says it was foreseeable.
This has happened before and the Government Accountability Office on September 14,
2026 predicted exactly this. They said without some major change, the FAA will once again repeat its
history of cost overruns and missed deadlines. They found there were 11,389 different project
schedules and there was no coordination. And what did the GAO conclude? That it will result
in air traffic outages and disruptions. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is
asking Congress for $50 billion for more upgrades. President Vladimir Zelensky reportedly said
Washington proposed the idea of Ukraine ceding land to Russia in exchange for NATO membership.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports. In comments reported by the AFP news agency, Zelensky said
the U.S. had asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from the eastern Donbass region if it is able to
join NATO. Zelensky said Ukraine is discussing specific security guarantees from NATO and the
European Union and that he would ask Ukrainians if they accepted the terms, if formally offered.
Meanwhile, Putin is maintaining his position that Ukraine hand over territory Russia does not
control and he's rejected any foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine. The Kremlin also renewed an
old demand that NATO pull back military infrastructure from central and eastern
European countries that joined NATO following the breakup of the Soviet Union. Eleanor Beardsley,
NPR News, Kyiv. Some Republican state officials are trying to revive the Trump administration's
push for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election, NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports.
More than a week after voting ended for this year's midterms, Missouri state
attorney general is leading 11 other Republican state officials in this push to shape the next
federal election in 2028. The U.S. Postal Service issued a revised mail-in ballot rule in August
in response to an executive order by President Trump. Under that rule, USPS would refuse to
deliver mail-in ballots to voters in states where election officials do not turn over their voter
list to the mailing agency. The Supreme Court blocked the USPS rule for the midterms. Now,
these Republican state officials are appealing a lower court order that's blocking USPS from
working on the rule for the 2028 election. U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols issued that order
after finding that the Postal Service likely has no authority to impose these requirements
on states. The Trump administration is not appealing the order. Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
It's NPR News. In Turkey, almost 200 countries are engaged in climate change negotiations,
but their goal of 11 years ago is out of reach, limiting global warming to 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit.
The planet is almost there as it burns fossil fuels. Now, the talks are about just how much
hotter it will get. The U.N. says on its current track, the world will warm by five degrees by
the end of the century. A new report details the circumstances surrounding the deaths of four
firefighters this summer near the Colorado-Utah border. The Mountain West News Bureau's
Murphy Woodhouse reports. Faced with rapidly approaching flames, five wildland firefighters
raced under their fire shelters for a shot at survival. Three died there, and a fourth died
a month later. Federal investigators say extreme fire behavior, communication breakdowns, staffing
shortages and other issues led to the tragedy. Former federal fire researcher Dave Cawkin praised
the report's detail, but said it failed to ask some key questions. All of this complexity
with that weather forecast suggested a need for somebody for a system to save action is not
feasible today. The Department of Interior, which released the report, did not immediately
respond to a request for comment. For NPR News, I'm Murphy Woodhouse. Amid airline difficulties,
there may be adjusted start times and different modes of transportation, but
weekend sports games will go on. Auburn University's football team took a bus to Mississippi State,
and today's start time was pushed back. The Big Ten said in a statement that all of its officials
had arrived for their scheduled assignments today. I'm Amy Helden Washington. This is NPR News.

topics.text: Nationwide ground stop exposes FAA air system vulnerabilities; L3Harris contractor error blamed
GAO warned in September 2026 that FAA upgrade delays and coordination failures would cause outages
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy seeks $50 billion from Congress for air traffic system upgrades
Zelensky says U.S. asked if Ukraine would cede Donbas for NATO membership; Kremlin repeats demands
Republican state officials appeal ruling blocking USPS mail-in ballot rule for the 2028 election
Global climate talks in Turkey acknowledge 2.7-degree warming goal is out of reach
Federal report details circumstances of four wildland firefighter deaths near Colorado-Utah border
Airline disruptions prompt schedule changes, but weekend college football games proceed as planned
